rows.rationale: Cited check meter threshold is superseded by later KERC regulations in KA-C5-006 setting the limit to 50kWp. | System capacity of 45 kW is below the 50 kW check meter requirement.
Proposed capacity is 45 kWp, which is not more than 50 kWp, so check meter is not required. | Clause relates to transformer capacity limits, which are deemed feasible up to 150 kW.
The cited clause is superseded by later GERC amendments. | Proposed DC capacity is 20 kW, which is not more than 20 kW, making check meters optional, yet approval was granted.
Proposed capacity is 20 kW, not exceeding 20 kW. Check meter is optional, so approval without a check meter is valid; however, cited rule threshold is misapplied.
The generator approved prematurely while portal status indicates technical feasibility outcome is not yet communicated by the licensee.
Cited clause 13.5 from 2016 regulations is superseded by the 2020 amendment regulations on the application date.
Cited clause DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 was superseded prior to the application date by the 2024 amendment.
Cited 2015 regulation is superseded by 2019 regulations on application date. | Proposed 1.0 kWp complies with the 2.0 kW load limit, making rejection factually invalid.

Superseded by newer BESCOM SOP KA-C5-006 setting the check meter threshold to 50 kWp for 80 kWp system.
Cited clause GJ-C3-001#cl-13.5-check was superseded on the application date. | System capacity is 12 kW (under 20 kW), making check meters optional, so rejection is invalid.

System capacity is 12 kW, which is under the 20 kW mandatory check meter threshold; rejection is invalid. | This clause governs meter accuracy classes, not check meter mandates, and does not support the rejection.

Cited rule DL-C3-004#cl-9.2b is superseded on the application date by DL-C3-015 allowing twice-yearly changes. | Applicable amended rule DL-C3-015#cl-9.2b permits changes twice a year with 2 months notice, which was met.
The application made 2 changes this financial year, which complies with the limit of twice per financial year under clause DL-C3-015#cl-9.2b.
Cited clause DL-C3-004#cl-3.8 was superseded before the application date by DL-C3-009.
Cited clause DL-C3-009#cl-3.6 was superseded by DL-C3-015#cl-3.6 on the application date.
Cumulative GNM capacity in BRPL is 50 MW, well within the 110 MW cap. Rejection based on capacity limit is factually incorrect.
Cited clause DL-C3-009#cl-3.6 was superseded prior to the application date of 2026-04-28.
Cumulative GNM capacity in TPDDL is 105 MW against the 100 MW cap under DL-C3-015#cl-3.6, making rejection valid.
The cited 2015 regulation was superseded by the UPERC Regulations, 2019 prior to the application date of 2023-09-16.

The installation is deemed feasible up to 150kW under Karnataka SOP, making technical verification unnecessary, but this specific applicable rule was omitted.

Cited clause DL-C3-006#cl-3.2 is superseded by the 2025 seventh amendment allowing VNM for all Delhi consumers. | Applicable current VNM rule DL-C3-015#cl-3.2 was ignored, making the rejection invalid.
The cited clause 3.8 regulates capacity caps for VNM (upto 5 times sanctioned load) and does not support a rejection decision.

Cited clause GJ-C3-003#cl-6.2 is superseded and not in force on the application date. | The cited rule allows capacity up to sanctioned load for captive consumers, making rejection incorrect for an 80kW plant on a 100kW load.
Cited clause is superseded on the application date.
The proposed capacity is 30kWp, while the check meter threshold is >50kWp; however, the correct SRTPV threshold for this system is >17.5kW under KA-C5-001#cl-15.
Cited rule 65% limit was amended by GJ-C3-003 to 100% of transformer capacity, making the old 65% proviso not in force on the application date.
The 65% limit was amended by GJ-C3-003 to 100%. Cumulative capacity of 70kW on a 100kVA transformer is compliant.
Portal status shows technical feasibility outcome was not communicated, yet generator incorrectly approved it before SDO verification.
